transcript: When I'm assessing a patient for hyaluronic acid injectables, I always begin by looking at the face, both at rest and in motion. Today, we're looking specifically at the nasolabial folds or laugh lines. It's the lines that extend from the sides of the nose towards the corners of the mouth. We're going to be treating them with Everlice. It's a hyaluronic acid injectable designed to correct moderate to severe dynamic facial wrinkles such as the nasolabial folds. So this is clearly what we're seeing at rest. You have some lines. At rest, I'm looking at the depth of the fold, the contour of the area, and whether there are any natural differences between the two sides of the face. But go ahead and just smile now, animate, okay. We want to make sure that when you do like smile, like some of these lines are not as obvious. This is an important part of my assessment because the face isn't static. As she smiles, I can see how these folds change with movement and where they become more pronounced. Relax again and smile one more time, perfect. When I'm assessing this area, I'm not simply looking at whether a line exists. I'm looking at its depth, how it changes with expression, the differences between each side and how it relates to the patient's natural facial movement. Everly smooth and Everly's form are hyaluronic acid injectables that can be used to correct moderate to severe dynamic facial wrinkles, including the nasolabial folds. Here we're using a softer product which is called Everly Smooth. What's nice about Everly Smooth is it's finer. We use it for fine lines. It will make such a nice difference. Which product I select and how I approach treatment depends on what I see during the individual patient's assessment. One of the most important things with hyaluronic acid injectables is knowing when enough is enough. My goal isn't to completely erase every fold or change the way someone's face naturally moves. These folds are part of the normal facial anatomy and expression. So instead I'm looking for areas where thoughtful correction can soften one's appearance while respecting the patient's natural features. So it's all about proportions.
